findings: No tested form makes either generic multiply function exact.
Target productShift stays in EBX while vs is spilled. Current native compiler retains vs in EBX and spills productShift.

Moving the accumulator OR from a pre-loop local into the loop condition restores the target0x4C frame and the argument-slot reuse for the combined flag, but leaves register allocation and switch-tail sharing different.
Signed-short vector views and a single64-bit cast per product generate identical code to their corresponding controls.
register productShift, long instead of int, bool flags, and a local shift copy do not change the inside-loop control body.
The ordinary wrapper forms reproduce the same48-byte candidate, with10 materialized bytes different due solely to two global loads emitted in reversed order.

Forwarding through the existing Opcode helper without inline changes the call and fails. Marking that helper inline restores the baseline wrapper but regresses two exact guest-program routines; it is rejected.
Reported differing-byte counts are positional full-body comparisons with verified relocation targets, not semantic-distance measures.
All controls use native VC7 compilation. No instructions or binary bytes were patched. No new behavioral equivalence claim is made for unpromoted probes.
The two valid FastMode header declaration-order controls leave all180 bodies unchanged.
Unsigned64 casts for mixed cases5/6 change tail sharing and restore1328 extent, but not the target register allocation or all target sharing. The same cast in unsigned-only case4 has no effect.
Compound product assignment does not change the corresponding180-function body hashes.

Later probes retain the frozen962213e baseline (160/180), while concurrent canonical work reached168/180. The unchanged179-function guarantee is relative to that frozen baseline; these probes are not claims about current canonical whole-DLL metrics.

Moving all controls before opcode decoding reproduces the first0x66 target bytes and the original frame/spill slots, but allocates EBX to accumulatorShift rather than productShift. No complete helper match results. Further shift declaration, initialization, case assignment, abs and cast controls do not resolve it.
Direct vt/vd expressions, delayed register fields, count/selector/flag expression controls and multiply bitfield views produce no new exact body. No canonical source promotion.

evidence.task: Independent source/control-flow review of generic Audio RSP multiply
evidence.finding: No semantic/control-flow omission identified; current flag/quantized widths supported. No source promoted.
structural_observations: Original keeps signed-signed and unsigned-unsigned IMUL paths separate, sharing only mixed-sign operand-load/multiply tail. Candidate merges most multiply paths and keeps vs in EBX instead of productShift.

Original VMACQ uses 32-bit quantized comparison but a 64-bit roundBit zero check. The emitted dead SAR does not imply quantized64; widening quantized introduces real high/low comparisons absent in original.
Original roundBit high zero occupies ESI, allowing positive rounding result to preserve it. Reusing result variable explicitly does not change candidate allocation.

conclusions.actual_typed_vector_views: Both bank-union and row-union full declarations, with signed/unsigned member loads and matching storage definitions, leave all180 function bodies identical to inside-OR control. All25 data objects retain exact contents.
conclusions.result_reuse_and_scope: Existing result as roundBit, or moving result declaration inside loop, leaves all180 bodies unchanged.
conclusions.quantized64: Rejected: adds two-word comparison branches absent from original, despite coincidental1328 extent.
conclusions.round32: Rejected: removes required two-word OR zero tests and does not restore ESI lifetime.

evidence.question: Why unsigned64 factor conversions alter generic multiply tail sharing
evidence: Original signed-signed and unsigned-unsigned cases have separate one-operand IMUL instructions; only mixed cases5/6 share the final unsigned load/IMUL.
Parent controls establish only mixed U64 factor conversions change emitted code; case4 unsigned64 cast alone is code-identical to inside-OR control.

Usual arithmetic conversion changes mixed expression type from signed64 to unsigned64. Negative signed16 values become modulo2^64 before multiplication; assigning resulting low64bits back to signed64 preserves this MSVC program's numeric product. This changes optimizer IR category even though native IMUL computes the same low64bits.

Late widening after signed32 multiplication is semantically valid for signed16×signed16 and signed16×unsigned16 ranges, but emits two-operand IMUL plus CDQ, unlike original. Explicit64-bit operands therefore have stronger evidence.
evidence.outcome: No exact candidate or promoted changes; register allocation still favors vs in EBX.
